claims.text: Dermatology AI models are trained predominantly on light-skinned, cancer-focused image collections.
claims.poster_quote: Dermatology AI models are trained predominantly on light-skinned, cancer-focused image collections.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Dermatology artificial intelligence (AI) models are trained predominantly on light-skinned, cancer-focused image collections.
claims.reason: This statement is explicitly stated in the abstract of the paper.

claims.text: HAM10000 and ISIC 2019 provide a Western, neoplastic source domain and in-domain reference.
claims.poster_quote: HAM10000 and ISIC 2019 provide a Western, neoplastic source domain and in-domain reference.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: HAM10000 [7] (10,015 dermoscopic images) and ISIC 2019 [10] (25,331 images) are pooled and mapped to a shared eight-class neoplastic taxonomy to train and evaluate the cancer baseline on familiar data.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly describes HAM10000 and ISIC 2019 as a Western, neoplastic source domain and in-domain reference.

claims.text: DDI holds diagnosis broadly fixed while varying Fitzpatrick skin-tone groups, isolating the tone effect.
claims.poster_quote: DDI holds diagnosis broadly fixed while varying Fitzpatrick skin-tone groups, isolating the tone effect.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: DDI (656 images; Fitzpatrick groups I-II, III-IV, V-VI) holds diagnosis broadly fixed while varying skin tone, isolating the tone effect; we use its binary malignant/benign label.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that DDI holds diagnosis broadly fixed while varying Fitzpatrick skin-tone groups to isolate the tone effect.

claims.text: SCIN is tone-diverse but dominated by non-neoplastic conditions absent from cancer training, isolating the disease-distribution effect.
claims.poster_quote: SCIN is tone-diverse but dominated by non-neoplastic conditions absent from cancer training, isolating the disease-distribution effect.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: SCIN [8] (6,517 images after cleaning; 3,061 patients) is tone-diverse but dominated by non-neoplastic conditions absent from cancer training data, isolating the distribution effect.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly describes SCIN as tone-diverse and dominated by non-neoplastic conditions, isolating the disease-distribution effect.

claims.text: DDI and SCIN are US-sourced proxies, not cohorts collected in resource-constrained settings.
claims.poster_quote: DDI and SCIN are US-sourced proxies, not cohorts collected in resource-constrained settings.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: DDI and SCIN are US-sourced proxies rather than RCS-collected cohorts; we return to this in Section 5.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that DDI and SCIN are US-sourced proxies and not cohorts collected in resource-constrained settings.

claims.text: The DDI analysis has only 55–77 test images per Fitzpatrick group.
claims.poster_quote: The DDI analysis has only 55–77 test images per Fitzpatrick group.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: First and most importantly, DDI and SCIN are US-sourced proxies used to isolate each factor, not RCS-collected data; our RCS conclusions are therefore inferential, and validation on genuinely RCS-collected cohorts is important future work. Second, the DDI tone analysis is statistically underpowered (55-77 images per Fitzpatrick group in the test split); we therefore avoid strong directional claims.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that the DDI analysis has only 55–77 test images per Fitzpatrick group.

claims.text: The DDI analysis is underpowered for strong directional claims.
claims.poster_quote: The DDI analysis is underpowered for strong directional claims.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Second, the DDI tone analysis is statistically underpowered (55-77 images per Fitzpatrick group in the test split); we therefore avoid strong directional claims.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that the DDI analysis is underpowered for strong directional claims.

claims.text: Tone and disease distribution are observed marginally rather than jointly.
claims.poster_quote: Tone and disease distribution are observed marginally rather than jointly.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Our design therefore observes the two axes marginally rather than jointly; the tone effect under shifted disease cannot be isolated in these datasets without confounding it with the change in label space, since DDI is scored on a binary task and SCIN on multi-class categories.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that tone and disease distribution are observed marginally rather than jointly.

claims.text: HAM10000 and ISIC 2019 contain 35,346 images.
claims.poster_quote: HAM10000 + ISIC 2019: 35,346 images; source and in-domain reference.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: HAM10000 [7] (10,015 dermoscopic images) and ISIC 2019 [10] (25,331 images) are pooled and mapped to a shared eight-class neoplastic taxonomy to train and evaluate the cancer baseline on familiar data.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that HAM10000 and ISIC 2019 contain 35,346 images in total.

claims.text: DDI contains 656 images.
claims.poster_quote: DDI: 656 images; tone-stratified evaluation using malignant/benign labels.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: DDI (656 images; Fitzpatrick groups I-II, III-IV, V-VI) holds diagnosis broadly fixed while varying skin tone, isolating the tone effect; we use its binary malignant/benign label.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that DDI contains 656 images.

claims.text: SCIN contains 6,517 images from 3,061 patients.
claims.poster_quote: SCIN: 6,517 images from 3,061 patients; tone-diverse, non-neoplastic distribution shift.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: SCIN [8] (6,517 images after cleaning; 3,061 patients) is tone-diverse but dominated by non-neoplastic conditions absent from cancer training data, isolating the distribution effect.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that SCIN contains 6,517 images from 3,061 patients.

claims.text: The adaptation correlation is based on four models.
claims.poster_quote: The adaptation correlation is based on four models.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The adaptation correlation is computed over four models and is descriptive rather than inferential.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that the adaptation correlation is based on four models.

claims.text: Only frozen features are evaluated.
claims.poster_quote: Only frozen features are evaluated; end-to-end or parameter-efficient fine-tuning may change the results.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: We evaluate four models as frozen feature extractors.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that only frozen features are evaluated.

claims.text: The cancer baseline and foundation models differ simultaneously in architecture, training objective, and pretraining scale.
claims.poster_quote: The cancer baseline and foundation models differ simultaneously in architecture, training objective, and pretraining scale, preventing complete isolation of specialization.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The cancer baseline differs from the foundation models in architecture, pretraining objective and pretraining scale simultaneously, so specialization cannot be fully isolated from these factors.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that the cancer baseline and foundation models differ in architecture, training objective, and pretraining scale.

claims.text: Accuracy is not chance-normalized across tasks with different class counts.
claims.poster_quote: Accuracy is not chance-normalized across tasks with different class counts, although the label-free purity analysis is chance-corrected.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Our accuracy comparison is not chance-normalized across tasks of differing class count (our chance-corrected label-free analysis is more directly comparable).
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that accuracy is not chance-normalized across tasks with different class counts.

claims.text: Embedding dimensionality differs by a factor of four and is not controlled in kNN purity.
claims.poster_quote: Embedding dimensionality differs by a factor of four and is not controlled in kNN purity.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: kNN purity is not controlled for embedding dimensionality, and the four encoders differ in dimensionality by a factor of four.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that embedding dimensionality differs by a factor of four and is not controlled in kNN purity.

claims.text: Mapping SCIN conditions into broad categories simplifies genuine diagnostic complexity.
claims.poster_quote: Mapping SCIN conditions into broad categories simplifies genuine diagnostic complexity.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The mapping of SCIN’s long tail into broad clinical categories simplifies genuine diagnostic complexity.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that mapping SCIN conditions into broad categories simplifies genuine diagnostic complexity.

claims.text: Fitzpatrick type measures UV response rather than pigmentation.
claims.poster_quote: Fitzpatrick type measures UV response rather than pigmentation, and additional dermatology foundation models remain to be tested.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Fitzpatrick type indexes UV response rather than pigmentation.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that Fitzpatrick type measures UV response rather than pigmentation.

claims.text: Disease-distribution shift is a larger and representationally grounded driver of failure than the matched-disease skin-tone effect.
claims.poster_quote: For the settings studied, disease-distribution shift is a larger and representationally grounded driver of failure than the matched-disease skin-tone effect.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Our results give a clear ordering of causes for the generalization gap in the settings studied: disease-distribution shift is a large, representationally grounded driver, whereas the matched-disease tone effect is small and inconsistent in direction.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that disease-distribution shift is a larger and representationally grounded driver of failure than the matched-disease skin-tone effect.

claims.text: Teams working under resource constraints may benefit more from selecting a broad dermatology-pretrained representation than from attempting to retrain a narrow cancer classifier.
claims.poster_quote: Teams working under resource constraints may benefit more from selecting a broad dermatology-pretrained representation than from attempting to retrain a narrow cancer classifier.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: First, model selection may matter more than local retraining: since recoverable performance is bounded by representation quality, teams may benefit from starting with a dermatology-pretrained foundation model rather than a cancer-specialized classifier.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly suggests that teams working under resource constraints may benefit more from selecting a broad dermatology-pretrained representation than from retraining a narrow cancer classifier.

claims.text: Roughly 10 examples per category recovered most attainable performance for the dermatology foundation models.
claims.poster_quote: Modest local labeling may suffice when the representation already contains target-condition structure: roughly 10 examples per category recovered most attainable performance for the dermatology foundation models.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: A few-shot probe with roughly ten labeled examples per local category recovered most attainable performance in our experiments.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that roughly 10 examples per category recovered most attainable performance for the dermatology foundation models.

claims.text: Adaptation is lightweight and runs on CPU.
claims.poster_quote: Adaptation is lightweight and runs on CPU; the main hardware demand is the one-time extraction of frozen embeddings.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The adaptation step itself is lightweight and runs on CPU, so the main hardware demand falls on the one-time feature extraction rather than on repeated local training.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that adaptation is lightweight and runs on CPU.

claims.text: Recoverable performance closely tracks pre-existing representation quality.
claims.poster_quote: Recoverable performance closely tracks pre-existing representation quality.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Recoverable performance closely tracks the label-free representation quality of Fig. 2 (r = 0.90 between SCIN purity lift and full-probe balanced accuracy across the four models).
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that recoverable performance closely tracks pre-existing representation quality.

claims.text: Across the four models, SCIN purity lift and full-probe balanced accuracy have a correlation of r = 0.90.
claims.poster_quote: Across the four models, SCIN purity lift and full-probe balanced accuracy have a correlation of r = 0.90.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Recoverable performance closely tracks the label-free representation quality of Fig. 2 (r = 0.90 between SCIN purity lift and full-probe balanced accuracy across the four models).
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that SCIN purity lift and full-probe balanced accuracy have a correlation of r = 0.90 across the four models.

claims.text: Linear probing uses L2-regularized logistic regression fitted on standardized frozen features.
claims.poster_quote: Linear probing: L2-regularized logistic regression is fitted on standardized frozen features using patient-level 70/30 splits to prevent leakage.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: We fit an L2-regularized logistic-regression probe on standardized frozen features, using patient-level GroupShuffleSplit (70/30) to prevent leakage, and report balanced accuracy.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that linear probing uses L2-regularized logistic regression fitted on standardized frozen features.

claims.text: Performance is reported as balanced accuracy.
claims.poster_quote: Performance is reported as balanced accuracy.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: We fit an L2-regularized logistic-regression probe on standardized frozen features, using patient-level GroupShuffleSplit (70/30) to prevent leakage, and report balanced accuracy.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that performance is reported as balanced accuracy.

claims.text: SCIN conditions are mapped into seven clinically grounded categories: inflammatory, infectious, vascular/purpuric, neoplastic, pigmentary, traumatic/other, and other.
claims.poster_quote: SCIN conditions are mapped into seven clinically grounded categories: inflammatory, infectious, vascular/purpuric, neoplastic, pigmentary, traumatic/other, and other.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: For SCIN, we map its long-tailed conditions into seven clinically grounded categories (inflammatory, infectious, vascular/purpuric, neoplastic, pigmentary, traumatic/other, and other) following standard dermatological grouping.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that SCIN conditions are mapped into seven clinically grounded categories.

claims.text: Cancer baseline full probe balanced accuracy is 0.21.
claims.poster_quote: Cancer baseline: 0.21 / 0.19 / 0.06
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The cancer baseline is strong in-domain (0.62) but degrades sharply on unfamiliar conditions (0.21 across categories; 0.06 at fine granularity).
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that the cancer baseline full probe balanced accuracy is 0.21.

claims.text: Cancer baseline 10-shot probe balanced accuracy is 0.19.
claims.poster_quote: Cancer baseline: 0.21 / 0.19 / 0.06
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The cancer baseline, lacking latent structure, recovers least (0.21) even with adaptation, whereas dermatology models recover substantially more, and for these models a few-shot probe with only ten labeled examples per category nearly matches or exceeds the full probe.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that the cancer baseline 10-shot probe balanced accuracy is 0.19.

claims.text: Cancer baseline purity lift is 0.06.
claims.poster_quote: Cancer baseline: 0.21 / 0.19 / 0.06
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On its home domain, the cancer baseline has the strongest representational structure of any model (purity lift +0.42), yet on SCIN its features barely separate conditions (+0.06) close to chance.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that the cancer baseline purity lift is 0.06.

claims.text: DermLIP full probe balanced accuracy is 0.36.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Dermatology foundation models degrade far less (DermLIP 0.36).
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that DermLIP full probe balanced accuracy is 0.36.

claims.text: DermLIP 10-shot probe balanced accuracy is 0.41.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Dermatology foundation models degrade far less (DermLIP 0.36), and for these models a few-shot probe with only ten labeled examples per category nearly matches or exceeds the full probe (DermLIP: 0.41 vs. 0.36).
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that DermLIP 10-shot probe balanced accuracy is 0.41.

claims.text: DermLIP purity lift is 0.23.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Dermatology foundation models retain three to four times more transferable structure under the same unfamiliar conditions (DermLIP +0.23).
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that DermLIP purity lift is 0.23.

claims.text: MONET full probe balanced accuracy is 0.34.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Dermatology foundation models degrade far less (DermLIP 0.36, MONET 0.34).
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that MONET full probe balanced accuracy is 0.34.

claims.text: MONET 10-shot probe balanced accuracy is 0.39.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Dermatology foundation models degrade far less (DermLIP 0.36), and for these models a few-shot probe with only ten labeled examples per category nearly matches or exceeds the full probe (DermLIP: 0.41 vs. 0.36; MONET: 0.39 vs. 0.34).
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that MONET 10-shot probe balanced accuracy is 0.39.

claims.text: MONET purity lift is 0.14.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Dermatology foundation models retain three to four times more transferable structure under the same unfamiliar conditions (DermLIP +0.23, MONET +0.14).
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that MONET purity lift is 0.14.

claims.text: DINOv3 full probe balanced accuracy is 0.31.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Even the no-dermatology control (DINOv3) transfers better than the cancer baseline (0.31 vs. 0.21 balanced accuracy).
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that DINOv3 full probe balanced accuracy is 0.31.

claims.text: DINOv3 10-shot probe balanced accuracy is 0.32.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: For these models a few-shot probe with only ten labeled examples per category nearly matches or exceeds the full probe (DermLIP: 0.41 vs. 0.36; MONET: 0.39 vs. 0.34; DINOv3: 0.32 vs. 0.31).
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that DINOv3 10-shot probe balanced accuracy is 0.32.

claims.text: DINOv3 purity lift is 0.16.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: DINOv3’s behavior deserves comment: with no dermatology pretraining it nonetheless transfers to SCIN better than the cancer baseline (0.31 vs. 0.21 balanced accuracy; +0.16 vs. +0.06 purity lift).
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that DINOv3 purity lift is 0.16.

claims.text: The cancer baseline has a kNN purity lift of +0.42 on its home domain.
claims.poster_quote: On its home domain, the cancer baseline has the strongest label-free structure, with a kNN purity lift of +0.42.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On its home domain, the cancer baseline has the strongest representational structure of any model (purity lift +0.42).
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that the cancer baseline has a kNN purity lift of +0.42 on its home domain.

claims.text: The cancer baseline has a kNN purity lift of +0.06 on SCIN.
claims.poster_quote: On SCIN, its features barely separate unfamiliar conditions, producing only +0.06 lift over chance.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On SCIN, its features barely separate conditions (+0.06) close to chance, demonstrating a genuine representational deficit rather than a missing output head.
claims.reason: Source location: Section 4.2, Figure 2. The paper explicitly states the cancer baseline has a kNN purity lift of +0.06 on SCIN.

claims.poster_quote: DermLIP: +0.23
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Dermatology foundation models retain three to four times more transferable structure under the same unfamiliar conditions (DermLIP +0.23).
claims.reason: Source location: Section 4.2, Figure 2. The paper explicitly states DermLIP has a SCIN purity lift of +0.23.

claims.text: MONET has a SCIN purity lift of +0.14.
claims.poster_quote: MONET: +0.14
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Dermatology foundation models retain three to four times more transferable structure under the same unfamiliar conditions (MONET +0.14).
claims.reason: Source location: Section 4.2, Figure 2. The paper explicitly states MONET has a SCIN purity lift of +0.14.

claims.text: DINOv3 has a SCIN purity lift of +0.16.
claims.poster_quote: DINOv3: +0.16
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: DINOv3’s behavior deserves comment: with no dermatology pretraining it nonetheless transfers to SCIN better than the cancer baseline (+0.16 vs. +0.06 purity lift).
claims.reason: Source location: Section 4.2, Figure 2. The paper explicitly states DINOv3 has a SCIN purity lift of +0.16.

claims.text: DermLIP retains nearly four times the transferable structure of the cancer baseline.
claims.poster_quote: DermLIP retains nearly four times the transferable structure of the cancer baseline.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Dermatology foundation models retain three to four times more transferable structure under the same unfamiliar conditions (DermLIP +0.23).
claims.reason: Source location: Section 4.2, Figure 2. The paper compares DermLIP's SCIN purity lift (+0.23) to the cancer baseline (+0.06), showing it retains nearly four times the transferable structure.

claims.text: The general-purpose DINOv3 model exceeds the cancer-specialized model despite lacking dermatology pretraining.
claims.poster_quote: The general-purpose DINOv3 model also exceeds the cancer-specialized model despite lacking dermatology pretraining.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: DINOv3’s behavior deserves comment: with no dermatology pretraining it nonetheless transfers to SCIN better than the cancer baseline (0.31 vs. 0.21 balanced accuracy; +0.16 vs. +0.06 purity lift).
claims.reason: Source location: Section 4.2. The paper explicitly states that DINOv3 exceeds the cancer baseline despite lacking dermatology pretraining.

claims.reason: Source location: Section 4.2. The paper explicitly states that specialization discards variation uninformative for melanoma-versus-nevus classification but essential for distinguishing conditions such as eczema and tinea.
